clue.text: Guitar sound always found in R&B

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: the music genre rhythm and blues, written with its two letters
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A guitarist notes that a certain echoing effect turns up on every rhythm and blues record.
explanation.walkthrough: The ampersand in R&B is ignored; only the R and the B are used, and they wrap round the word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb is the echo effect added to an electric guitar's signal, so it is a guitar sound.

clue.text: Wood regularly red-brown

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the hyphenated pair

explanation.surface: A description of timber with a reddish-brown colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen is ignored when counting letters; starting with the second letter gives the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a poetic or archaic name for ebony, a dark hardwood.

clue.text: Provocative pieces stir up race riot given Trump's leadership

indicators.note: to stir something up is to agitate and mix it, so these letters are churned into a new order
a leader goes in front, so leadership here means taking only the opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: Inflammatory material whips up racial unrest under a demagogue's lead, a political headline.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all politics, but 'Provocative pieces' turns out to mean works of art designed to arouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Works intended to arouse desire are provocative pieces in the sexual sense of provocative.

clue.text: Contrarian advice from Spooner's short sellers?

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the starting sounds of words, so his name signals that swap

blocks.note: shy means short of something, and bears are traders who sell short, betting on a fall

explanation.surface: A financial tip that goes against what the market's pessimists are doing.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of 'shy bears' to get the answer. A bear on the stock market sells shares expecting prices to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: When everyone is selling, a contrarian investor recommends doing the opposite and purchasing stock.

clue.text: I understand you're going to diet around Xmas

indicators.note: understanding by ear: what the setter hears said, rather than reads, is the source here
turned around means moved about, so these letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: 'you will' contracted, which is how you say 'you're going to'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges a friend's plan to slim down over the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I understand' reads as sympathy, but it signals a sound-alike: 'you'll' is said like YULE. 'Around' looks like 'about the time of' but jumbles the diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is an old name for the Christmas season, which Xmas abbreviates.

clue.text: "Hello! BB's little sister Joanna, I presume?"

blocks.note: a presumption about who someone is, put as 'you must be...'
Jo is the short, little form of the name Joanna
BB King, the blues guitarist; his sister would share his surname

explanation.surface: A greeting to a stranger, in the style of 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?', guessing she is a famous musician's sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the four clues with no definition. The joke is an imaginary Jo King, sister of the bluesman, greeted with 'You must be Jo King'.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble says this clue carries no definition; the phrase is a standard expression of disbelief.

clue.text: Neil Diamond's original remixed, with added material

indicators.note: the original is what comes first, so only the opening letter is used
a remix reworks a recording into a new version, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the surname

explanation.surface: A record producer reissues a Neil Diamond song in a new mix with extra tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer's name is split: his first name is used whole, his surname only for its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment or box that is lined has an extra layer of material fixed inside it.

clue.text: Hotel concierge cuddles phone operator

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold close in an embrace, so the words around enclose what is sought

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A hotel's concierge gets very friendly with a switchboard worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phone operator' suggests a person at a switchboard, but it means a company providing telephone service.
explanation.definitionFit: Telco is a short informal name for a telecommunications company, which operates phone networks.

clue.text: Cooked without oil, oven-glazed with Merlot?

blocks.note: first meaning: heated in an oven or pan with no fat added, as with nuts
second, playful meaning: done in the oven with a coating of a wine that is not sweet

explanation.surface: A recipe note: the dish is cooked fat-free, then glazed with red wine in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: Merlot is a dry red wine, and roasting is oven cooking, so a joint glazed with it is roasted in something dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry-roasted food, peanuts especially, is cooked by dry heat with no fat or liquid involved.

clue.text: Appeal to Blair: our little girl is stuck in New York

indicators.note: something stuck in a place is lodged inside it, so the earlier pieces go within the later one

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for the city and state
an appeal addressed to Tony Blair, the former British prime minister, in the old vocative form 'O Tony'
taken as written
Nell is a short, little form of a girl's name such as Eleanor or Helen

explanation.surface: A plea to a prime minister about a daughter trapped in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the four clues with no definition. The two letters of the city split to hold everything else; 'O' before a name is the old poetic way of calling on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble says this clue carries no definition; the phrase is a British idiom for an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Loudish, funny clown on the radio

indicators.note: funny can mean odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order
radio carries only sound, so what is wanted is a word that is heard, not seen

blocks.note: taken as written
Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown in Britain

explanation.surface: A rather noisy comic clown performing on a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the four clues with no definition. 'Funny' sits beside 'clown' as if describing it, but it shuffles the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble says this clue carries no definition; the phrase is dated British slang meaning 'certainly not'.

clue.text: Police car despatched to guard Republican function

indicators.note: something despatched is sent off and broken up from where it was, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
a guard stands round what it protects, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A squad car is sent out to protect a party political event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party event in the surface, but it is the mathematical sense. The mixed letters hold R between their fifth and sixth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the reciprocal, one divided by x, is a standard function.

clue.text: Live broadcast screening lavish opening scene of Sunset Boulevard?

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so just the first letter of the word is wanted
a screen stands around and shields something, so the pair encloses a piece

blocks.note: to live is to be, to exist
to air a programme is to broadcast it
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A TV channel shows live the lavish opening scene of the classic Hollywood film Sunset Boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make Sunset Boulevard the film, but here it is the actual road in Los Angeles; the question mark admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel Air is a wealthy Los Angeles neighbourhood that the real Sunset Boulevard runs through, so it is a location along it.

clue.text: It's used to blow up magazine we clad in iron

indicators.note: something clad in a material is covered all over by it, so one piece is wrapped by another

blocks.note: Time is a well-known American news magazine
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
we, in the object form

explanation.surface: Someone describes an armour-plated store of explosives and its detonating mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' suggests an ammunition store, which fits the explosive surface, but it is a periodical. 'We' must become its object form to fit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A time fuse sets off a bomb after a set delay, so it is a device for detonating explosives.

clue.text: Front two of Manchester United struggling to eclipse the primacy of Giggs' greatness

indicators.note: the front pair of a word are its opening couple of letters
primacy means being first, so only the first letter is wanted
a team that is struggling is in disarray, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the first letters of the city's name: its first two
the first letter of the surname
taken as written

explanation.surface: Manchester United's strike pair find it hard to outshine the brilliance of Ryan Giggs, the club's legendary winger.
explanation.walkthrough: The G is mixed in with the other letters; the jumbled word together with it is placed after the opening pair of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnitude means size or importance, which is the same idea as greatness.

clue.text: Overweight rebel takes over South Africa's ruling party

indicators.note: to take something over is to take it in and hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: fat means overweight
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
the African National Congress, which has governed South Africa since 1994

explanation.surface: A portly insurgent seizes control of South Africa's governing party.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the four clues with no definition. The famous revolutionary known by his first name opens up to hold the party's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble says this clue carries no definition; the phrase is an ironic idiom meaning there is no possibility at all.

clue.text: A lack of appreciation for girl's discernment

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana; with the possessive it becomes Di's
taste is discernment in judging what is good

explanation.surface: Someone fails to value a young woman's good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stays in the wordplay as a letter S, a common crossword liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is dislike or aversion, the opposite of enjoying or valuing something.

clue.text: Flicker, like a candle in Oscar's observatory?

blocks.note: first meaning: a candle flame wavers and runs with melted wax
second meaning: Oscar Wilde said we all lie in a low place, though some of us look up at the stars from it

explanation.surface: A candle's flame wavers inside some astronomical observatory belonging to someone called Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half alludes to Oscar Wilde's line about looking at the stars from the gutter, so that street drain is where he does his stargazing.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle is said to gutter when its flame flickers and wax runs down, and Wilde's stargazers sit in a roadside drain.

clue.text: Gloss over Roman Polanski's background

blocks.note: first meaning: to give furniture a high shine with shellac
second meaning: the film director holds French and Polish heritage and citizenship

explanation.surface: Someone skates over the troubled past of the film director Roman Polanski.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloss over' reads as 'avoid discussing', which fits Polanski's notorious history, but here it means to finish wood. Polanski was born in Paris to Polish parents.
explanation.definitionFit: French polishing is a technique for giving wooden furniture a glossy surface, and the director's nationality is French-Polish.

clue.text: African people exercise during sun's retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back the way one came, so the word runs backwards
something happening during a period falls within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
taken as written; the apostrophe-s ties it to the next word

explanation.surface: People in Africa work out while the sun is going down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun's retreat' suggests sunset, but the word itself goes backwards and takes the exercise inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nupe are an ethnic group of central Nigeria, so Nupes are an African people.

clue.text: Destination for Hispaniola vacation I note

indicators.note: to vacate is to empty, so the word loses its middle and keeps only its ends

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
taken as written
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt te

explanation.surface: A traveller names a Caribbean island holiday spot and jots it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destination for Hispaniola' reads as one phrase, but 'Destination' alone is the definition; 'Vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptying the island's name out.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti, the country on the western part of Hispaniola, is a place a traveller might head to.

clue.text: Observe one involved in cyber espionage?

blocks.note: first meaning: to catch sight of
second, playful meaning: an online spy, with the E- prefix used for electronic things like email

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: like e-commerce and e-book, an e-spy would be a spy working electronically.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or spot something, which is to see it at a distance.

clue.text: The unpredictable nature of madcap US conspiracies!

indicators.note: madcap means wildly reckless, so the letters are thrown about crazily

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how wild and erratic American conspiracy theories are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madcap' looks like an adjective for the theories, and it is; it also tells you to mix up the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Capriciousness means a tendency to sudden whims and changes of mood, which is being unpredictable.

clue.text: Red wine addict introduced to bin end of Riesling

indicators.note: something introduced to a place is put into it, so one piece goes inside another
the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a lush is a drunkard
the last letter of the grape name

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker is shown the cut-price oddments bin of red wine and German Riesling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red wine' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'Red' is the definition and 'wine addict' is the wordplay. A bin end is a cheap last bottle of a wine line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blushing goes red in the face from embarrassment, so the adjective matches.

clue.text: Man still defending Londonderry extremists

indicators.note: a defender surrounds what it protects, so one piece encloses the other
the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, at either end

blocks.note: even can mean still, as in 'even better' meaning 'still better'
the first and last letters of the city name

explanation.surface: A man is still defending militant hardliners in the Northern Ireland city of Londonderry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' looks political in the surface but only asks for the city's end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn can be a man's name, as with the novelist Evelyn Waugh, so it fits a generic male.
